${\text{5 moles of A}}^{\text{n+}} = \left(\text{5-n}\right){\text{moles of MnO}_{4}^{-}$
$\dfrac{\text{5}}{\text{5-n}} = \dfrac{\text{2.68} \times 1 {0}^{- 3}}{\text{1.61} \times {\text{10}}^{- 3}} = \text{1.66} = \dfrac{\text{5}}{\text{3}}$
$5 - \text{n} = 3$
$∴ \text{n} = 2$

questions.q:
Select the nature or type of redox change in the following reaction:-

${Cl}_{2} \to {ClO}^{-} + {Cl}^{-}$
questions.solution:
Auto-redox or disproportionation is the one in which same substance is oxidized and reduced as well.

Intramolecular redox change is the one in which one element of a compound is oxidized and the other element is reduced.

Intermolecular redox is the one in which one of the two reactants is oxidized and the other is reduced.

questions.q:
What will be the value of x, y and $z$ in the following equation?
${H}_{2}{C}_{2}{O}_{4} + x{H}_{2}{O}_{2} \to yC{O}_{2} + z{H}_{2}O$
questions.solution:
(i) The half reaction for oxidation is,
${H}_{2}{C}_{2}{O}_{4} \to C{O}_{2}$
Balancing carbon atoms on both sides, ${H}_{2}{C}_{2}{O}_{4} \to 2C{O}_{2}$
Balancing hydrogen atoms on both sides, ${H}_{2}{C}_{2}{O}_{4} \to 2C{O}_{2} + 2H^{+}$
Balancing the charge on both sides,
${H}_{2}{C}_{2}{O}_{4} \to 2C{O}_{2} + 2H^{+} + 2e^{-}$...(i)
(ii) The half reaction for reduction is‐ ${H}_{2} {O}_{2} \to {H}_{2} \text{O}$
Balancing oxygen atoms on both sides, ${H}_{2}{O}_{2} \to 2{H}_{2}O$
Balancing hydrogen atoms, ${H}_{2}{O}_{2} + 2H^{+} \to 2{H}_{2}O$
Balancing the charge,
${H}_{2}{O}_{2} + 2H^{+} + 2e^{-} \to 2{H}_{2}O$...(ii)
Now, adding both equations, ${H}_{2}{C}_{2}{O}_{4} + {H}_{2}{O}_{2} \to 2C{O}_{2} + 2{H}_{2}O$
This is balanced equation so x, y, z are 1,2,2 respectively.

questions.q: All the following species are strong oxidizing agents. Their strength as oxidizing agents in acidic solution is such that
questions.solution:
The standard reduction potentials of the above species in acidic medium are as given below
${S}_{2}{O}_{8}^{2 -} ( aq ) + 2e^{-} \to 2S{O}_{4}^{2 -} ( aq ) ; E ° = + 2.01\text{V}$
$Mn{O}_{4}^{-} ( aq ) + 8H^{+} + 5e^{-} \to Mn^{2 +} ( aq ) + 4{H}_{2}O; E ° = + 1.77\text{V}$
$C{r}_{2}{O}_{7}^{2 -} ( aq ) + 14H^{+} + 6e^{-} \to 2Cr^{3 +} + 7{H}_{2}O; E ° = + 1.33\text{V}$
The more the standard reduction potential, the more the tendency of the species to undergo reduction and more strongly it (species) would work as oxidizing agent.
As a result, their strength as oxidizing agent in acidic solution decreases in the following order
${S}_{2}{O}_{8}^{2 -} > Mn{O}_{4}^{-} > C{r}_{2}{O}_{7}^{2 -}$

questions.q: A compound contains three elements X, Y and Z. The oxidation number of X, Y and Z are $+ 3, + 5$ and $- 2$ respectively. The possible formula of the compound is
questions.solution:
The sum of all oxidation values must be equal to zero. Let, number of atoms of X, Y and Z are respectively a, b and c.

Then, $( + 3 ) ext{a} + ( + 5 ) ext{b} + ( - 2 ) ext{c} = 0$

Or

$3 ext{a} + 5 ext{b} - 2 ext{c} = 0$

Now, putting values of a, b and c for all the given options, which will give sum equal to zero, will be our formula.

(a) For, ${ ext{X}_{2} ext{Y} ext{Z}$

$ ext{a} = 2$

$ ext{b} = 1$

$ ext{c} = 1$

Thus, $3 ext{a} + 5 ext{b} - 2 ext{c} = 0$

$3 imes 2 + 5 - 2 e 0$

(b) For, $ ext{X} ext{Y}{ ext{Z}_{3}$

$ ext{a} = 1, ext{b} = 1, ext{c} = 3$

$3 ext{a} + 5 ext{b} - 2 ext{c} = 0$

$3 + 5 - 6 e 0$

(c) ${ ext{X}_{3}{( ext{Y}{ ext{Z}_{4} )}_{3}$

$ ext{a} = 3, ext{b} = 3, ext{c} = 12$

$3 ext{a} + 5 ext{b} - 2 ext{c} = 0$

$( 3 imes 3 + 5 imes 3 ) - ( 2 imes 12 ) = 0$

$9 + 15 - 24$

$24 - 24 = 0$

(d) ${ ext{X}_{2}{ ext{Y}_{2} ext{Z}$

$ ext{a} = 2, ext{b} = 2, ext{c} = 1$

$3 ext{a} + 5 ext{b} - 2 ext{c} = 0$

$( 3 imes 2 ) + ( 5 imes 2 ) - ( 2 imes 1 ) = 0$

$6 + 10 - 2 e 0$

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.
